question: At the moment, the Prime Minister of Spain, Pedro Sánchez, is beset with countless corruption cases involving his wife and brother, his party, and his government.

The Guardia Civil (UCO) recently sent a report to the courts showing that Pedro Sánchez was personally aware of and gave the green light to a face-to-face meeting between José Luis Ábalos, PSOE organisational secretary and Minister for Transport, and Delcy Rodríguez, on European soil, disregarding the sanctions that the European Union imposed on Delcy Rodríguez.

The audacity José Luis Ábalos and Pedro Sánchez showed and the impunity with which they acted are extremely serious and affect the security of the entire continent, together with Spain’s credibility and prestige. 1.
Will the Council open a serious and in-depth investigation and impose personal sanctions on Sánchez and others involved? I would like to reiterate the questions I asked the Council (E-000468/2020)1:
What tools can the institutions use to ensure adherence to decisions 2017/2074 and 2018/901 when a Member State government chooses to breach them?
Will the matter of Venezuela and its dangerous relationship with the Spanish left-wing government be on the agenda at the next Council meeting?
answer: As outlined in the reply to Written Question E-000468/2020, under Article 29 TEU, Member States must ensure that their national policies conform to the Union positions; this includes the provisions in Council decisions concerning restrictive measures under the common foreign and security policy (CFSP).

It is the responsibility of each Member State concerned to ensure that these measures are properly applied in any given case. The Foreign Affairs Council has discussed the situation in Venezuela at several of its meetings, most recently on 14 October 2024. It will continue to do so as appropriate.
